overview: This three-page file concerns Taiwan’s commercial and agricultural relations with the Philippines and the United States under Japanese colonial rule in 1940. Its principal document is a despatch from American Consul Gerald Warner reporting a Taiwan Chamber of Commerce sample fair in Manila, where a small delegation displayed products including tea, camphor, canned foods, coral, liquor, bamboo goods, and clothing in an effort to stimulate trade. A subsequent State Department memorandum summarizes Agricultural Attaché Owen L. Dawson’s difficulties obtaining Taiwanese agricultural statistics because Japanese military authorities restricted the release of recent and historical data, and raises the possibility of seeking reciprocal access to information.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the Manila Sample Fair of Taiwan Products
subfiles.about: Reports on a Taiwan Chamber of Commerce delegation that exhibited Taiwanese products at a sample fair in Manila during April and May 1940.
subfiles.summary: The Taiwan Chamber of Commerce originally planned to send about twelve prominent businessmen to Manila, but foreign-exchange difficulties involving the Finance Ministry reduced the delegation to George Makoto Ohyi, M. Mori, Y. Goto, and G. Ueda. They displayed approximately 2,000 pesos’ worth of Taiwanese goods, including coral, tea, camphor, canned foods, alcoholic beverages, bamboo products, handicrafts, perfumes, and clothing. Although the delegation generated little immediate business and gave away most of its samples, it regarded the first-of-its-kind fair as a useful step toward stimulating trade. Ohyi also reported helpful treatment by Manila immigration and customs officials and recounted an unnamed Filipino trade minister’s interest in reproducing Taiwanese products under similar Philippine climatic conditions.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Restrictions Affecting Agricultural Reporting from Taiwan
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes Agricultural Attaché Owen L. Dawson’s report on Japanese military restrictions limiting access to agricultural information in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum abstracts Shanghai telegram no. 3128 of May 9, 1940, which transmitted Owen L. Dawson’s account of an official trip to Taiwan. Dawson attributed difficulty obtaining statistics and other information to a military ruling barring disclosure of figures for the previous two years and, in many cases, older basic data without express permission. He suggested that continued restrictions might warrant asking Japanese authorities for freer access on the basis of reciprocity for information supplied to Japan by the United States and the Philippines. Despite these obstacles, he judged the trip valuable.

interest: The file juxtaposes two revealing dimensions of Taiwan’s wartime colonial economy: active Japanese-sponsored promotion of Taiwanese goods in Southeast Asia and increasing military secrecy surrounding agricultural data. The Manila despatch is especially useful for its detailed commodity list, identification of individual delegation members, and account of Filipino interest in transferring Taiwanese production methods. The June memorandum shows how economic intelligence gathering was being constrained before the Pacific War and records an American impulse to use informational reciprocity in negotiations with Japan.
